questions.prompt: Which samples should be used to fit the baseline mean predictor?
questions.explanation: The baseline is a model too; fitting it on test data would leak.

questions.prompt: A linear fit's residuals plotted against x form a clear U shape. What is the most likely cause?
options: The learning rate is too small for the optimiser to converge
The data have too few samples to compute a meaningful mean
The relationship is curved and the model is missing a feature
The bias term has been penalised by the regulariser
questions.explanation: Residuals should look patternless; structure means unmodelled systematic effects.

questions.prompt: In ridge regression, why is the bias usually left out of the penalty?
options: The bias is an offset, not a sensitivity; shrinking it distorts predictions
The bias is always exactly zero after the features have been scaled
Penalising the bias would make the loss function non-convex
The bias has no gradient, so the optimiser cannot change it
questions.explanation: Weights are shrunk to reduce sensitivity; the offset must stay free to match the mean target.

questions.prompt: Why is the least-squares solution a good test for a gradient-descent implementation?
options: It applies to every neural network, whatever its architecture
It is an independent exact answer that the iterates must approach
It is always faster than gradient descent for any model
It never needs a design matrix, unlike gradient descent
questions.explanation: Agreement between two independent methods catches sign and scaling bugs.
